# Lab 8.3: Incremental Tables

## What We Are Going to Do
Build an incremental table that only processes new rows on each run, with a unique key so changed rows are merged.

## Steps

1. **[Console] Create the incremental model.** `definitions/marts/order_items_inc.sqlx`:


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">config {
  type: "incremental",
  uniqueKey: ["id"],
  bigquery: { partitionBy: "DATE(created_at)", updatePartitionFilter: "created_at &gt;= TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 7 DAY)" }
}

pre_operations {
  DECLARE max_ts DEFAULT (
    ${when(incremental(), `SELECT MAX(created_at) FROM ${self()}`, `SELECT TIMESTAMP("2000-01-01")`)}
  )
}

SELECT id, order_id, product_id, status, sale_price, created_at
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.order_items`
WHERE created_at &gt; max_ts</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[Console] First run.** Execute only this action (**Start execution → Selection of actions**). The first run builds the full table.

3. **[Console] Second run.** Execute it again. Open the action's **Details** in Executions: the compiled SQL is now a `MERGE` that only reads rows newer than `max_ts`.

4. **[Console] Full refresh.** Start an execution with **Run with full refresh** ticked. The table is rebuilt from scratch.

5. **[CLI] Compare the jobs.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false \
'SELECT creation_time, statement_type, total_bytes_processed
 FROM `region-us`.INFORMATION_SCHEMA.JOBS_BY_PROJECT
 WHERE query LIKE "%order_items_inc%" ORDER BY creation_time DESC LIMIT 5'</span>
</code></pre>

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| First run | Full build |
| Later runs | `MERGE` of new rows only |
| `uniqueKey` | Updates rows that already exist |
| Full refresh | Rebuilds when logic changes |
